Hero.subtitle: Hi, I'm Muhammad Naufal Arif. I graduated in Information Systems and currently work at the intersection of AI data infrastructure and web development. I care deeply about how things are built under the hood.

gpa.title: Academic Foundation
gpa.description: Information Systems graduate from STT Terpadu Nurul Fikri. Learned how to map logic into systems.

qa.title: AI Data Infrastructure
qa.description: Auditing 3D point clouds and spatial data to ensure autonomous models learn from reality.

web.title: Web Development
web.description: Writing servers, wiring databases, and building interfaces that just work.

jobs.description: I act as the final line of defense for a Tier-1 autonomous driving dataset. My daily work revolves around auditing complex 3D LiDAR point clouds and enforcing strict spatial boundaries. It taught me that an algorithm is only as smart as the data we feed it.
I did the groundwork for 3D spatial mapping. I spent hours meticulously labeling point clouds into 40+ object categories, making sure the environment boundaries didn't bleed into one another.
My introduction to AI data infrastructure. I tracked dynamic objects and traffic signs across 4D spatio-temporal datasets. Keeping Object IDs consistent across frames required pixel-perfect accuracy.
Before entering tech, I worked in operations. I cross-verified corporate documents and monitored physical inventory movements. It trained my eyes to catch discrepancies early.
I built a point-of-sale system from scratch for a local distributor. Using Node.js and SQLite, I learned how to translate messy business requirements into a functional tool people use every day.

lidar.title: 3D LiDAR Spatial QA
lidar.desc: I audited and annotated complex 3D point clouds for autonomous driving datasets. Enforcing strict spatial boundaries and zero defects taught me that an AI is only as smart as the data it learns from.

dialectica.title: Dialectica
dialectica.desc: A digital library interface I built using Next.js. I integrated the Gemini API so users could chat about the books they read. The hardest part was keeping the AI's context window relevant during long discussions.

ecommerce.title: E-commerce Product Catalog
ecommerce.desc: A freelance collaboration where I helped develop a product management system. We used Laravel 12 and Livewire to keep the frontend reactive without writing a ton of custom JavaScript.

uwais.title: Uwais Point of Sale
uwais.desc: The first actual enterprise tool I engineered. It handles automated invoicing and tracks inventory. Keeping the database queries fast on a local SQLite file was a fun challenge.

kostku.title: Kostku Property Finder
kostku.desc: I stepped into a Project Manager role for this one. We built a React.js property search interface. It taught me a lot about Agile cycles and why communicating with designers is just as important as writing code.

forum.title: Discussion Forum API
forum.desc: A purely backend project. I wrote a REST API for a forum that handles user authentication and nested comments securely.

rental.title: Car Rental System
rental.desc: A database-heavy application for managing rental periods and user sessions, built on the classic CodeIgniter framework.

ai.title: Data Infrastructure
ai.desc: 3D LiDAR mapping, semantic segmentation, bounding box tracking, and strict quality assurance.

web.title: Web Engineering
web.desc: TypeScript, React (Next.js), Node.js, Laravel, and everything in between.

data.title: Storage & Deployment
data.desc: MySQL, PostgreSQL, SQLite, Git, and deploying on platforms like Vercel.

cert.title: Workflow
cert.desc: Agile cycles, rapid prototyping, and reading through endless documentation.
